confirmed.statement: The t-tests compare people, not ideas. I took each Table 1 t statistic (2 decimals) with its P value (exact P from Figures 2a and 2b and appendix pp. 28-30 where printed) and solved for the degrees of freedom. Every test with |t| of 1.5 or more gives a df interval inside 35 to 83, and each interval overlaps the Welch range for 31 and 30 people (29 to 59). Tests on the 3302 ideas would have df in the hundreds. Day 2 Task 2 usefulness (t = -4.23, P = 8.2e-05) needs df of at least 58.1. A Welch df cannot exceed N - 2, so all 61 people entered that test.

summary: Every people count in the form matches the PDF: 61 students were enrolled and randomly assigned (31 ChatGPT, 30 control) and the same 61 completed the seven-day lab (pp. 3-4), and the Table 1 note (N=61), the 427 = 61 x 7 solutions, the 30 blue and 31 red solution dots in Figure 4b panels B1 and B7, and the t-test degrees of freedom (up to 58, which needs all 61 people) all agree, so S1 alone clears 50. Caveats that change no count: the paper never states how many took the Day 30 follow-up (the Day 30 novelty test implies at least 53), and, outside this lens, the form's note that the markdown stops at PDF p. 17 is out of date.
